scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A big plane can weigh hundreds of tonnes. Yet it floats on thin air. What holds it up?

scenes.name: thrust
scenes.text: First, the engines push the plane forward fast. Around two hundred and fifty kilometres per hour, for take off.

scenes.name: wing
scenes.text: The wings are curved, and tilted slightly upward, at an angle to the oncoming air.

scenes.name: down
scenes.text: The wing deflects huge amounts of air downward. Push air down, and the air pushes the wing up. Newton's third law.

scenes.name: press
scenes.text: Air also speeds up over the curved top, so pressure there drops, while pressure below stays higher. That difference is lift.

scenes.name: forces
scenes.text: When lift beats weight, and thrust beats drag, the plane climbs. In cruise, they all balance.

scenes.name: flaps
scenes.text: For take off and landing, flaps slide out, making the wing bigger and more curved, for extra lift at low speed.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Thrust, wings, air down, lift. Physics, not magic. Follow for more on how things really work.
